# Document: handleOpen

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810174-handleopen
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810174-handleopen
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# handleOpen

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Controls the open / close behavior of an IOService object (overrideable by subclasses).

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual bool handleOpen(
 IOService *forClient, 
 IOOptionBits options, 
 void *arg ); 
```

## Parameters

- `forClient`: Designates the client of the provider requesting the open.
- `options`: Options for the open, may be interpreted by the implementor of `handleOpen`.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

`true`if the open was successful; `false` otherwise.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

IOService calls this method in its subclasses in response to the open method, so the subclass may implement the request. The default implementation provides single owner access to an IOService object via `open`. The object is locked via lockForArbitration before `handleOpen` is called.

# Document: initialPowerStateForDomainState

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810182-initialpowerstatefordomainstate
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810182-initialpowerstatefordomainstate
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# initialPowerStateForDomainState

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Determines which power state a device is in, given the current power domain state.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual unsigned long initialPowerStateForDomainState(
 IOPMPowerFlagsdomainState ); 
```

## Parameters

- `domainState`: Flags that describe the character of "domain power"; they represent the `outputPowerCharacter` field of a state in the power domain's power state array.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

A state number.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Power management calls this method once, when the driver is initializing power management. Most drivers do not need to implement this method, and can rely upon the default IOService implementation. The IOService implementation scans the power state array looking for the highest state whose `inputPowerRequirement` field exactly matches the value of the `domainState` parameter. If more intelligent determination is required, the power managed driver should implement the method and override the superclass's implementation.

# Document: isInactive

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810198-isinactive
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810198-isinactive
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# isInactive

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Checks if the IOService object has been terminated, and is in the process of being destroyed.

## Declaration

```objectivec
bool isInactive(
 void ) const; 
```

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

`true` if the IOService object has been terminated.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

When an IOService object is successfully terminated, it is immediately made inactive, which blocks further attach()es, matching or notifications occuring on the object. It remains inactive until the last client closes, and is then finalized and destroyed.

# Document: isOpen

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810209-isopen
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810209-isopen
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# isOpen

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Determines whether a specific, or any, client has an IOService object open.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual bool isOpen(
 const IOService *forClient = 0 ) const; 
```

## Parameters

- `forClient`: If non-zero, \<codeisOpenreturns the open state for that client. If zero is passed, \<codeisOpenreturns the open state for all clients.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

\<codetrueif the specific, or any, client has the IOService object open.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Returns the open state of an IOService object with respect to the specified client, or when it is open by any client.

# Document: joinPMtree

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810216-joinpmtree
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810216-joinpmtree
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# joinPMtree

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Joins the driver into the power plane of the I/O Registry.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual void joinPMtree(
 IOService *driver ); 
```

## Parameters

- `driver`: The driver to be added to the power plane, usually `this`.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

A driver uses this method to call its nub when initializing (usually in its `start` routine after calling PMinit), to be attached into the power management hierarchy (i.e., the power plane). A driver usually calls this method on the driver for the device that provides it power (this is frequently the nub). Before this call returns, the caller will probably be called at setPowerParent and setAggressiveness and possibly at addPowerChild as it is added to the hierarchy. This method may be overridden by a nub subclass.

# Document: lockForArbitration

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810228-lockforarbitration
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810228-lockforarbitration
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# lockForArbitration

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Locks an IOService object against changes in state or ownership.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual bool lockForArbitration(
 bool isSuccessRequired = true ); 
```

## Parameters

- `isSuccessRequired`: If a request for access to an IOService object should be denied if it is terminated, pass `false`, otherwise pass `true`.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

The registration, termination and open / close functions of IOService use `lockForArbtration` to single-thread access to an IOService object. `lockForArbitration` grants recursive access to the same thread.

# Document: makeUsable

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810246-makeusable
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810246-makeusable
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# makeUsable

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Requests that a device become usable.

## Declaration

```objectivec
IOReturn makeUsable(
 void ); 
```

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

A return code that can be ignored by the caller.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

This method is called when some client of a device (or the device's own driver) is asking for the device to become usable. Power management responds by telling the object upon which this method is called to change to its highest power state. `makeUsable` is implemented using changePowerStateToPriv. Subsequent requests for lower power, such as from `changePowerStateToPriv`, will pre-empt this request.

# Document: mapDeviceMemoryWithIndex

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810261-mapdevicememorywithindex
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810261-mapdevicememorywithindex
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# mapDeviceMemoryWithIndex

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Maps a physical range of a device.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual IOMemoryMap * mapDeviceMemoryWithIndex(
 unsigned intindex, 
 IOOptionBits options = 0 ); 
```

## Parameters

- `index`: An index into the array of ranges assigned to the device.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

An instance of IOMemoryMap, or zero if the index is beyond the count available. The mapping should be released only when access to it is no longer required.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

This method creates a mapping for the IODeviceMemory at the given index, with `IODeviceMemory::map(options)`. The mapping is represented by the returned instance of IOMemoryMap, which should not be released until the mapping is no longer required.

# Document: matchLocation

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810275-matchlocation
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810275-matchlocation
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# matchLocation

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Allows a registered IOService object to direct location matching.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual IOService * matchLocation(
 IOService *client ); 
```

## Parameters

- `client`: The IOService object at which matching is taking place.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

Returns the IOService instance to be used for location matching.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

By default, a location matching property will be applied to an IOService object's provider. This method allows that behavior to be overridden by families.

# Document: matchPropertyTable

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810286-matchpropertytable
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810286-matchpropertytable
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# matchPropertyTable

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Allows a registered IOService object to implement family specific matching.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual bool matchPropertyTable(
 OSDictionary *table, 
 SInt32 *score ); 
```

## Parameters

- `table`: The dictionary of properties to be matched against.
- `score`: Pointer to the current driver's probe score, which is used to order multiple matching drivers in the same match category. It defaults to the value of the `IOProbeScore` property in the drivers property table, or `kIODefaultProbeScore` if none is specified.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

`false` if the family considers the matching dictionary does not match in properties it understands; `true` otherwise.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

All matching on an IOService object will call this method to allow a family writer to implement matching in addition to the generic methods provided by IOService. The implementer should examine the matching dictionary passed to see if it contains properties the family understands for matching, and use them to match with the IOService object if so. Note that since matching is also carried out by other parts of the I/O Kit, the matching dictionary may contain properties the family does not understand - these should not be considered matching failures.

# Document: maxCapabilityForDomainState

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810302-maxcapabilityfordomainstate
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810302-maxcapabilityfordomainstate
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# maxCapabilityForDomainState

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Determines a driver's highest power state possible for a given power domain state.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual unsigned long maxCapabilityForDomainState(
 IOPMPowerFlagsdomainState ); 
```

## Parameters

- `domainState`: Flags that describe the character of "domain power"; they represent the `outputPowerCharacter` field of a state in the power domain's power state array.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

A state number.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

This happens when the power domain is changing state and power management needs to determine which state the device is capable of in the new domain state. Most drivers do not need to implement this method, and can rely upon the default IOService implementation. The IOService implementation scans the power state array looking for the highest state whose `inputPowerRequirement` field exactly matches the value of the `domainState` parameter. If more intelligent determination is required, the driver itself should implement the method and override the superclass's implementation.

# Document: message

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810323-message
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810323-message
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# message

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Receives a generic message delivered from an attached provider.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual IOReturn message(
 UInt32 type,
 IOService *provider, 
 void *argument = 0 ); 
```

## Parameters

- `type`: A type defined in `IOMessage.h` or defined by the provider family.
- `provider`: The provider from which the message originates.
- `argument`: An argument defined by the provider family, not used by IOService.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

An IOReturn code defined by the message type.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

A provider may deliver messages via the `message` method to its clients informing them of state changes, such as `kIOMessageServiceIsTerminated` or `kIOMessageServiceIsSuspended`. Certain messages are defined by the I/O Kit in `IOMessage.h` while others may be family dependent. This method is implemented in the client to receive messages.

# Document: messageClient

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810334-messageclient
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810334-messageclient
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# messageClient

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Sends a generic message to an attached client.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual IOReturn messageClient(
 UInt32 messageType,
 OSObject *client, 
 void *messageArgument = 0,
 vm_size_t argSize = 0 ); 
```

## Parameters

- `messageType`: A type defined in `IOMessage.h` or defined by the provider family.
- `client`: A client of the IOService to send the message.
- `messageArgument`: An argument defined by the provider family, not used by IOService.
- `argSize`: Specifies the size of messageArgument, in bytes. If argSize is non-zero, messageArgument is treated as a pointer to argSize bytes of data. If argSize is 0 (the default), messageArgument is treated as an ordinal and passed by value.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

The return code from the client message call.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

A provider may deliver messages via the message method to its clients informing them of state changes, such as `kIOMessageServiceIsTerminated` or `kIOMessageServiceIsSuspended`. Certain messages are defined by the I/O Kit in `IOMessage.h` while others may be family dependent. This method may be called in the provider to send a message to the specified client, which may be useful for overrides.

# Document: messageClients

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810353-messageclients
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810353-messageclients
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# messageClients

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Sends a generic message to all attached clients.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual IOReturn messageClients(
 UInt32 type, 
 void *argument = 0,
 vm_size_t argSize = 0 ); 
```

## Parameters

- `type`: A type defined in `IOMessage.h` or defined by the provider family.
- `argument`: An argument defined by the provider family, not used by IOService.
- `argSize`: Specifies the size of argument, in bytes. If argSize is non-zero, argument is treated as a pointer to argSize bytes of data. If argSize is 0 (the default), argument is treated as an ordinal and passed by value.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

Any non-`kIOReturnSuccess` return codes returned by the clients, or `kIOReturnSuccess` if all return `kIOReturnSuccess`.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

A provider may deliver messages via the message method to its clients informing them of state changes, such as `kIOMessageServiceIsTerminated` or `kIOMessageServiceIsSuspended`. Certain messages are defined by the I/O Kit in `IOMessage.h` while others may be family dependent. This method may be called in the provider to send a message to all the attached clients, via the messageClient method.

# Document: nameMatching(const char *, OSDictionary *)

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810365-namematching
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810365-namematching
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# nameMatching(const char \*, OSDictionary \*)

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Creates a matching dictionary, or adds matching properties to an existing dictionary, that specify an IOService name match.

## Declaration

```objectivec
static OSDictionary * nameMatching(
 const char *name, 
 OSDictionary *table = 0 ); 
```

## Parameters

- `name`: The service's name, as a const C string. Name matching is successful on IOService objects that respond successfully to the `IORegistryEntry::compareName` method.
- `table`: If zero, `nameMatching` creates a matching dictionary and returns a reference to it, otherwise the matching properties are added to the specified dictionary.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

The matching dictionary created, or passed in, is returned on success, or zero on failure.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

A very common matching criteria for IOService object is based on its name. `nameMatching` creates a matching dictionary that specifies any IOService object which responds successfully to the IORegistryEntry::compareName method. An existing dictionary may be passed in, in which case the matching properties will be added to that dictionary rather than creating a new one.

# Document: nameMatching(const OSString *, OSDictionary *)

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810383-namematching
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810383-namematching
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# nameMatching(const OSString \*, OSDictionary \*)

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Creates a matching dictionary, or adds matching properties to an existing dictionary, that specify an IOService name match.

## Declaration

```objectivec
static OSDictionary * nameMatching(
 const OSString *name, 
 OSDictionary *table = 0 ); 
```

## Parameters

- `name`: The service's name, as an OSString (which includes OSSymbol). Name matching is successful on IOService objects that respond successfully to the `IORegistryEntry::compareName` method.
- `table`: If zero, `nameMatching` creates a matching dictionary and returns a reference to it, otherwise the matching properties are added to the specified dictionary.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

The matching dictionary created, or passed in, is returned on success, or zero on failure.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

A very common matching criteria for IOService object is based on its name. `nameMatching` creates a matching dictionary that specifies any IOService object which responds successfully to the IORegistryEntry::compareName method. An existing dictionary may be passed in, in which case the matching properties will be added to that dictionary rather than creating a new one.

# Document: newUserClient

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810417-newuserclient
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810417-newuserclient
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# newUserClient

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Creates a connection for a non kernel client.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual IOReturn newUserClient(
 task_towningTask,
 void *securityID, 
 UInt32type,
 OSDictionary *handler, 
 IOUserClient **properties ); 
```

## Parameters

- `owningTask`: The Mach task of the client thread in the process of opening the user client. Note that in macOS, each process is based on a Mach task and one or more Mach threads. For more information on the composition of a Mach task and its relationship with Mach threads, see [Tasks and Threads](https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/Darwin/Conceptual/KernelProgramming/Mach/Mach.html#//apple_ref/doc/uid/TP30000905-CH209-TPXREF103).
- `securityID`: A token representing the access level for the task.
- `type`: A constant specifying the type of connection to be created, specified by the caller of [IOServiceOpen](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/iokit/1514515-ioserviceopen) and interpreted only by the family.
- `handler`: An instance of an IOUserClient object to represent the connection, which will be released when the connection is closed, or zero if the connection was not opened.
- `properties`: A dictionary of additional properties for the connection.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

A return code to be passed back to the caller of `IOServiceOpen`.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

A non kernel client may request a connection be opened via the [IOServiceOpen](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/iokit/1514515-ioserviceopen) library function, which will call this method in an IOService object. The rules and capabilities of user level clients are family dependent, and use the functions of the IOUserClient class for support. IOService's implementation returns `kIOReturnUnsupported`, so any family supporting user clients must implement this method.

# Document: nextIdleTimeout

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810435-nextidletimeout
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810435-nextidletimeout
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# nextIdleTimeout

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Allows subclasses to customize idle power management behavior.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual SInt32 nextIdleTimeout(
 AbsoluteTimecurrentTime, 
 AbsoluteTimelastActivity,
 unsigned intpowerState); 
```

## Parameters

- `currentTime`: The current time
- `lastActivity`: The time of last activity on this device
- `powerState`: The device's current power state.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

Returns the next time the device should idle off (in seconds, relative to the current time).

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Returns the next time that the device should idle into its next lower power state. Subclasses may override for custom idle behavior.

A power managed driver might override this method to provide a more sophisticated idle power off algorithm than the one defined by power management.

# Document: open

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810450-open
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810450-open
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# open

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Requests active access to a provider.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual bool open(
 IOService *forClient, 
 IOOptionBits options = 0, 
 void *arg = 0 ); 
```

## Parameters

- `forClient`: Designates the client of the provider requesting the open.
- `options`: Options for the open. The provider family may implement options for open; IOService defines only `kIOServiceSeize` to request the device be withdrawn from its current owner.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

`true` if the open was successful; `false` otherwise.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

IOService provides generic open and close semantics to track clients of a provider that have established an active datapath. The use of `open` and close, and rules regarding ownership are family defined, and defined by the handleOpen and handleClose methods in the provider. Some families will limit access to a provider based on its open state.

Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# PMinit

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Initializes power management for a driver.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual void PMinit(
 void ); 
```

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

`PMinit` allocates and initializes the power management instance variables, and it should be called before accessing those variables or calling the power management methods. This method should be called inside the driver's `start` routine and must be paired with a call to PMstop. Most calls to `PMinit` are followed by calls to joinPMtree and registerPowerDriver.

# Document: PMstop

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810502-pmstop
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810502-pmstop
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# PMstop

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Stop power managing the driver.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual void PMstop(
 void ); 
```

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Removes the driver from the power plane and stop its power management. This method is synchronous against any power management method invocations (e.g. `setPowerState` or `setAggressiveness`), so when this method returns it is guaranteed those power management methods will not be entered. Driver should not call any power management methods after this call. Calling `PMstop` cleans up for the three power management initialization calls: PMinit, joinPMtree, and registerPowerDriver.

## See Also

### Miscellaneous

- [acknowledgePowerChange](1809710-acknowledgepowerchange.md): Acknowledges an in-progress power state change.
- [acknowledgeSetPowerState](1532596-acknowledgesetpowerstate.md): Acknowledges the belated completion of a driver’s setPowerState power state change.
- [activityTickle](1809731-activitytickle.md): Informs power management when a power-managed device is in use, so that power management can track when it is idle and adjust its power state accordingly.
- [addLocation](1809740-addlocation.md): Adds a location matching property to an existing dictionary.
- [addMatchingNotification](1809749-addmatchingnotification.md): Adds a persistant notification handler to be notified of IOService events.

# Document: powerChangeDone

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810518-powerchangedone
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810518-powerchangedone
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# powerChangeDone

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Tells a driver when a power state change is complete.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual void powerChangeDone(
 unsigned longstateNumber ); 
```

## Parameters

- `stateNumber`: The number of the state in the state array that the device has switched from.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Power management uses this method to inform a driver when a power change is completely done, when all interested parties have acknowledged the powerStateDidChangeTo call. The default implementation of this method is null; the method is meant to be overridden by subclassed power managed drivers. A driver should use this method to find out if a power change it initiated is complete.

# Document: powerOverrideOffPriv

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810533-poweroverrideoffpriv
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810533-poweroverrideoffpriv
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# powerOverrideOffPriv

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Allows a driver to disable a power override.

## Declaration

```objectivec
IOReturn powerOverrideOffPriv(
 void ); 
```

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

A return code that can be ignored by the caller.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

When a driver has enabled an override via powerOverrideOnPriv, it can disable it again by calling this method in its superclass. Disabling the override reverts to the default algorithm for determining a device's power state. The superclass will now keep the device at the highest state required by `changePowerStateTo`, `changePowerStateToPriv`, and its children. Turning off the override will initiate a power change if the driver's desired power state is different from the maximum of the power managed driver's desire and the children's desires.

# Document: powerOverrideOnPriv

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810549-poweroverrideonpriv
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810549-poweroverrideonpriv
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# powerOverrideOnPriv

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Allows a driver to ignore its children's power management requests and only use changePowerStateToPriv to define its own power state.

## Declaration

```objectivec
IOReturn powerOverrideOnPriv(
 void ); 
```

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

A return code that can be ignored by the caller.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Power management normally keeps a device at the highest state required by its requests via changePowerStateTo, changePowerStateToPriv, and its children. However, a driver may ensure a lower power state than otherwise required by itself and its children using `powerOverrideOnPriv`. When the override is on, power management keeps the device's power state in the state specified by `changePowerStateToPriv`. Turning on the override will initiate a power change if the driver's `changePowerStateToPriv` desired power state is different from the maximum of the `changePowerStateTo` desired power state and the children's desires.

# Document: powerStateDidChangeTo

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810564-powerstatedidchangeto
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810564-powerstatedidchangeto
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# powerStateDidChangeTo

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Informs interested parties that a device has changed to a different power state.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual IOReturn powerStateDidChangeTo( 
 IOPMPowerFlagscapabilities, 
 unsigned longstateNumber, 
 IOService *whatDevice ); 
```

## Parameters

- `capabilities`: Flags that describe the capability of the device in the new power state (they come from the `capabilityFlags` field of the new state in the power state array).
- `stateNumber`: The number of the state in the state array that the device is switching to.
- `whatDevice`: A pointer to the driver that is changing. It can be used by a driver that is receiving power state change notifications for multiple devices to distinguish between them.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

The driver returns `IOPMAckImplied` if it has prepared for the power change when it returns. If it has started preparing but not finished, it should return a number of microseconds which is an upper limit of the time it will need to finish preparing. Then, when it has completed its preparations, it should call acknowledgePowerChange.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Power management informs interested parties that a device has changed to a different power state. Interested parties are those that have registered for this notification via registerInterestedDriver. If you have called `registerInterestedDriver` on a power managed driver, you must implemnt powerStateWillChangeTo and `powerStateDidChangeTo` to receive the notifications. `powerStateDidChangeTo` is called in a clean and separate thread context. `powerStateWillChangeTo` is called before a power state transition takes place; `powerStateDidChangeTo` is called after the transition has completed.

# Document: powerStateForDomainState

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810576-powerstatefordomainstate
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810576-powerstatefordomainstate
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# powerStateForDomainState

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Determines what power state the device would be in for a given power domain state.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual unsigned long powerStateForDomainState(
 IOPMPowerFlagsdomainState ); 
```

## Parameters

- `domainState`: Flags that describe the character of "domain power"; they represent the `outputPowerCharacter` field of a state in the power domain's power state array.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

A state number.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Power management calls a driver with this method to find out what power state the device would be in for a given power domain state. This happens when the power domain is changing state and power management needs to determine the effect of the change. Most drivers do not need to implement this method, and can rely upon the default IOService implementation. The IOService implementation scans the power state array looking for the highest state whose `inputPowerRequirement` field exactly matches the value of the `domainState` parameter. If more intelligent determination is required, the power managed driver should implement the method and override the superclass's implementation.

# Document: powerStateWillChangeTo

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810597-powerstatewillchangeto
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810597-powerstatewillchangeto
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# powerStateWillChangeTo

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Informs interested parties that a device is about to change its power state.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual IOReturn powerStateWillChangeTo( 
 IOPMPowerFlagscapabilities, 
 unsigned longstateNumber, 
 IOService *whatDevice ); 
```

## Parameters

- `capabilities`: Flags that describe the capability of the device in the new power state (they come from the `capabilityFlags` field of the new state in the power state array).
- `stateNumber`: The number of the state in the state array that the device is switching to.
- `whatDevice`: A pointer to the driver that is changing. It can be used by a driver that is receiving power state change notifications for multiple devices to distinguish between them.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

The driver returns `IOPMAckImplied` if it has prepared for the power change when it returns. If it has started preparing but not finished, it should return a number of microseconds which is an upper limit of the time it will need to finish preparing. Then, when it has completed its preparations, it should call acknowledgePowerChange.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Power management informs interested parties that a device is about to change to a different power state. Interested parties are those that have registered for this notification via registerInterestedDriver. If you have called `registerInterestedDriver` on a power managed driver, you must implement `powerStateWillChangeTo` and powerStateDidChangeTo to receive the notifications. `powerStateWillChangeTo` is called in a clean and separate thread context. `powerStateWillChangeTo` is called before a power state transition takes place; `powerStateDidChangeTo` is called after the transition has completed.

# Document: probe

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810605-probe
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810605-probe
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# probe

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

During an IOService object's instantiation, probes a matched service to see if it can be used.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual IOService * probe(
 IOService *provider, 
 SInt32 *score ); 
```

## Parameters

- `provider`: The registered IOService object that matches a driver personality's matching dictionary.
- `score`: Pointer to the current driver's probe score, which is used to order multiple matching drivers in the same match category. It defaults to the value of the `IOProbeScore` property in the drivers property table, or `kIODefaultProbeScore` if none is specified. The `probe` method may alter the score to affect start order.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

An IOService instance or zero when the probe is unsuccessful. In almost all cases the value of `this` is returned on success. If another IOService object is returned, the probed instance is detached and freed, and the returned instance is used in its stead for `start`.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

The registration process for an IOService object (the provider) includes instantiating possible driver clients. The `probe` method is called in the client instance to check the matched service can be used before the driver is considered to be started. Since matching screens many possible providers, in many cases the `probe` method can be left unimplemented by IOService subclasses. The client is already attached to the provider when `probe` is called.

# Document: propertyMatching

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810622-propertymatching
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810622-propertymatching
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# propertyMatching

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Creates a matching dictionary, or adds matching properties to an existing dictionary, that specify an IOService phandle match.

## Declaration

```objectivec
static OSDictionary * propertyMatching(
 const OSSymbol *key,
 const OSObject *value, 
 OSDictionary *table = 0 ); 
```

## Parameters

- `key`: The service's phandle, as a const UInt32. PHandle matching is successful on IOService objects that respond successfully to the IORegistryEntry method compareName.
- `value`: The service's phandle, as a const UInt32. PHandle matching is successful on IOService's which respond successfully to the IORegistryEntry method compareName.
- `table`: If zero, nameMatching will create a matching dictionary and return a reference to it, otherwise the matching properties are added to the specified dictionary.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

The matching dictionary created, or passed in, is returned on success, or zero on failure.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

A very common matching criteria for IOService is based on its name. nameMatching will create a matching dictionary that specifies any IOService which respond successfully to the IORegistryEntry method compareName. An existing dictionary may be passed in, in which case the matching properties will be added to that dictionary rather than creating a new one.

Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# publishResource(const char \*, OSObject \*)

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Uses the resource service to publish a property.

## Declaration

```objectivec
static void publishResource(
 const char *key,
 OSObject *value = 0 ); 
```

## Parameters

- `key`: A C string key that globally identifies the object.
- `The`: object to be published.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

The resource service uses IOService object's matching and notification to allow objects to be published and found by any I/O Kit client by a global name. `publishResource` makes an object available to anyone waiting for it or looking for it in the future.

# Document: registerInterestedDriver

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810675-registerinteresteddriver
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810675-registerinteresteddriver
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# registerInterestedDriver

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Allows an IOService object to register interest in the changing power state of a power-managed IOService object.

## Declaration

```objectivec
IOPMPowerFlags registerInterestedDriver(
 IOService *theDriver ); 
```

## Parameters

- `theDriver`: The driver of interest adds this pointer to the list of interested drivers. It informs drivers on this list before and after the power change.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

Flags describing the capability of the device in its current power state. If the current power state is not yet defined, zero is returned (this is the case when the driver is not yet in the power domain hierarchy or hasn't fully registered with power management yet).

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Call `registerInterestedDriver` on the IOService object you are interested in receiving power state messages from, and pass a pointer to the interested driver (`this`) as an argument. The interested driver is retained until the power interest is removed by calling `deRegisterInterestedDriver`. The interested driver should override powerStateWillChangeTo and powerStateDidChangeTo to receive these power change messages. Interested drivers must acknowledge power changes in `powerStateWillChangeTo` or `powerStateDidChangeTo`, either via return value or later calls to acknowledgePowerChange.

# Document: registerInterrupt

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810691-registerinterrupt
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810691-registerinterrupt
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# registerInterrupt

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Registers a C function interrupt handler for a device supplying interrupts.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual IOReturn registerInterrupt(
 int source,
 OSObject *target, 
 IOInterruptAction handler, 
 void *refCon = 0); 
```

## Parameters

- `source`: The index of the interrupt source in the device.
- `target`: An object instance to be passed to the interrupt handler.
- `handler`: The C function to be called at primary interrupt time when the interrupt occurs. The handler should process the interrupt by clearing the interrupt, or by disabling the source.
- `refCon`: A reference constant for the handler's use.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

An IOReturn code.

`kIOReturnNoInterrupt` is returned if the source is not valid; `kIOReturnNoResources` is returned if the interrupt already has an installed handler.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

This method installs a C function interrupt handler to be called at primary interrupt time for a device's interrupt. Only one handler may be installed per interrupt source. IOInterruptEventSource provides a work loop based abstraction for interrupt delivery that may be more appropriate for work loop based drivers.

# Document: registerPowerDriver

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810706-registerpowerdriver
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810706-registerpowerdriver
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# registerPowerDriver

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Registers a set of power states that the driver supports.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual IOReturn registerPowerDriver( 
 IOService *controllingDriver, 
 IOPMPowerState *powerStates, 
 unsigned longnumberOfStates ); 
```

## Parameters

- `controllingDriver`: A pointer to the calling driver, usually `this`.
- `powerStates`: A driver-defined array of power states that the driver and device support. Power states are defined in `pwr_mgt/IOPMpowerState.h`.
- `numberOfStates`: The number of power states in the array.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

IOPMNoErr. All errors are logged via `kprintf`.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

A driver defines its array of supported power states with power management in its power management initialization (its `start` routine). If successful, power management will call the driver to instruct it to change its power state through setPowerState. Most drivers do not need to override `registerPowerDriver`. A nub may override `registerPowerDriver` if it needs to arrange its children in the power plane differently than the default placement, but this is uncommon.

# Document: registerService

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810726-registerservice
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810726-registerservice
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# registerService

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Starts the registration process for a newly discovered IOService object.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual void registerService(
 IOOptionBits options = 0 ); 
```

## Parameters

- `options`: The default zero options mask is recommended and should be used in most cases. The registration process is usually asynchronous, with possible driver probing and notification occurring some time later. `kIOServiceSynchronous` may be passed to carry out the matching and notification process for currently registered clients before returning to the caller.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

This function allows an IOService subclass to be published and made available to possible clients, by starting the registration process and delivering notifications to registered clients. The object should be completely setup and ready to field requests from clients before `registerService` is called.

# Document: registryEntryIDMatching

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810750-registryentryidmatching
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810750-registryentryidmatching
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# registryEntryIDMatching

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Creates a matching dictionary, or adds matching properties to an existing dictionary, that specify a IORegistryEntryID match.

## Declaration

```objectivec
static OSDictionary * registryEntryIDMatching(
 uint64_t entryID, 
 OSDictionary *table = 0 ); 
```

## Parameters

- `name`: The service's ID. Matching is successful on the IOService object that return that ID from the `IORegistryEntry::getRegistryEntryID()` method.
- `table`: If zero, `registryEntryIDMatching` creates a matching dictionary and returns a reference to it, otherwise the matching properties are added to the specified dictionary.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

The matching dictionary created, or passed in, is returned on success, or zero on failure.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

`registryEntryIDMatching` creates a matching dictionary that specifies the IOService object with the assigned registry entry ID (returned by `IORegistryEntry::getRegistryEntryID()`). An existing dictionary may be passed in, in which case the matching properties will be added to that dictionary rather than creating a new one.

Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# removePowerChild

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Informs a power managed driver that one of its power plane childen is disappearing.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual IOReturn removePowerChild(
 IOPowerConnection *theChild ); 
```

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

This call is handled internally by power management. It is not intended to be overridden or called by drivers.

# requestPowerDomainState

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Tells a driver to adjust its power state.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual IOReturn requestPowerDomainState( 
 IOPMPowerFlags desiredState, 
 IOPowerConnection *whichChild, 
 unsigned long specificationFlags ); 
```

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

# requestProbe

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Requests that hardware be re-scanned for devices.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual IOReturn requestProbe(
 IOOptionBitsoptions ); 
```

## Parameters

- `options`: Family defined options, not interpreted by IOService.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

An IOReturn code.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

For bus families that do not usually detect device addition or removal, this method represents an external request (eg. from a utility application) to rescan and publish or remove found devices.

# Document: requestTerminate

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810819-requestterminate
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810819-requestterminate
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# requestTerminate

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Passes a termination up the stack.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual bool requestTerminate(
 IOService *provider,
 IOOptionBitsoptions ); 
```

## Parameters

- `provider`: The terminated provider of this object.
- `options`: Options originally passed to terminate, plus `kIOServiceRecursing`.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

`true` if this object should be terminated now that its provider has been.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

When an IOService is made inactive the default behavior is to also make any of its clients that have it as their only provider also inactive, in this way recursing the termination up the driver stack. This method allows an IOService object to override this behavior. Returning `true` from this method when passed a just terminated provider will cause the client to also be terminated.

# Document: resourceMatching(const char *, OSDictionary *)

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810840-resourcematching
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810840-resourcematching
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# resourceMatching(const char \*, OSDictionary \*)

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Creates a matching dictionary, or adds matching properties to an existing dictionary, that specify a resource service match.

## Declaration

```objectivec
static OSDictionary * resourceMatching(
 const char *name, 
 OSDictionary *table = 0 ); 
```

## Parameters

- `name`: The resource name, as a const C string. Resource matching is successful when an object by that name has been published with the `publishResource` method.
- `table`: If zero, `resourceMatching` creates a matching dictionary and returns a reference to it, otherwise the matching properties are added to the specified dictionary.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

The matching dictionary created, or passed in, is returned on success, or zero on failure.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

IOService maintains a resource service IOResources that allows objects to be published and found globally in the I/O Kit based on a name, using the standard IOService matching and notification calls.

# Document: serviceMatching(const char *, OSDictionary *)

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810880-servicematching
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810880-servicematching
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# serviceMatching(const char \*, OSDictionary \*)

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Creates a matching dictionary, or adds matching properties to an existing dictionary, that specify an IOService class match.

## Declaration

```objectivec
static OSDictionary * serviceMatching(
 const char *className, 
 OSDictionary *table = 0 ); 
```

## Parameters

- `className`: The class name, as a const C string. Class matching is successful on IOService objects of this class or any subclass.
- `table`: If zero, `serviceMatching` creates a matching dictionary and returns a reference to it, otherwise the matching properties are added to the specified dictionary.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

The matching dictionary created, or passed in, is returned on success, or zero on failure.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

A very common matching criteria for IOService object is based on its class. `serviceMatching` creates a matching dictionary that specifies any IOService object of a class, or its subclasses. The class is specified by name, and an existing dictionary may be passed in, in which case the matching properties will be added to that dictionary rather than creating a new one.

# Document: setAggressiveness

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810925-setaggressiveness
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810925-setaggressiveness
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# setAggressiveness

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Broadcasts an aggressiveness factor from the parent of a driver to the driver.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual IOReturn setAggressiveness( 
 unsigned longtype, 
 unsigned longnewLevel ); 
```

## Parameters

- `type`: The aggressiveness factor type, such as `kPMMinutesToDim`, `kPMMinutesToSpinDown`, `kPMMinutesToSleep`, and `kPMPowerSource`. (Aggressiveness factors are defined in `pwr_mgt/IOPM.h`.)
- `newLevel`: The aggressiveness factor's new value.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

`IOPMNoErr`.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Implement `setAggressiveness` to receive a notification when an "aggressiveness Aggressiveness factors are a loose set of power management variables that contain values for system sleep timeout, display sleep timeout, whether the system is on battery or AC, and other power management features. There are several aggressiveness factors that can be broadcast and a driver may take action on whichever factors apply to it. A driver that has joined the power plane via joinPMtree will receive `setAgressiveness` calls when aggressiveness factors change. A driver may override this call if it needs to do something with the new factor (such as change its idle timeout). If overridden, the driver must call its superclass's `setAgressiveness` method in its own `setAgressiveness` implementation. Most drivers do not need to implement `setAgressiveness`.

# setDeviceMemory

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Sets the array of IODeviceMemory objects representing a device's memory mapped ranges.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual void setDeviceMemory(
 OSArray *array ); 
```

## Parameters

- `array`: An OSArray of IODeviceMemory objects, or zero if none are available. The array will be retained by the object.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

This method sets an array of IODeviceMemory objects representing the physical memory ranges allocated to a memory mapped device.

# Document: setIdleTimerPeriod

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810962-setidletimerperiod
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810962-setidletimerperiod
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# setIdleTimerPeriod

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Sets or changes the idle timer period.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual IOReturn setIdleTimerPeriod(
 unsignedperiod ); 
```

## Parameters

- `period`: The desired idle timer period in seconds.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

`kIOReturnSuccess` upon success; an I/O Kit error code otherwise.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

A driver using the idleness determination provided by IOService calls its superclass with this method to set or change the idle timer period. See activityTickle for a description of this type of idleness determination.

# Document: start

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1811009-start
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1811009-start
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# start

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

During an IOService object's instantiation, starts the IOService object that has been selected to run on the provider.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual bool start(
 IOService *provider ); 
```

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

`true` if the start was successful; `false` otherwise (which will cause the instance to be detached and usually freed).

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

The `start` method of an IOService instance is called by its provider when it has been selected (due to its probe score and match category) as the winning client. The client is already attached to the provider when `start` is called.

Implementations of `start` must call `start` on their superclass at an appropriate point. If an implementation of `start` has already called `super::start` but subsequently determines that it will fail, it must call `super::stop` to balance the prior call to `super::start` and prevent reference leaks.

# Document: stop

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1811034-stop
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1811034-stop
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# stop

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

During an IOService termination, the stop method is called in its clients before they are detached & it is destroyed.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual void stop(
 IOService *provider ); 
```

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

The termination process for an IOService (the provider) will call stop in each of its clients, after they have closed the provider if they had it open, or immediately on termination.

Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# stringFromReturn

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Supplies a programmer-friendly string from an IOReturn code.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual const char * stringFromReturn(
 IOReturnrtn ); 
```

## Parameters

- `rtn`: The IOReturn code.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

A pointer to a constant string, or zero if the return code is unknown.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Strings are available for the standard return codes in `IOReturn.h` in IOService, while subclasses may implement this method to interpret family dependent return codes.

# Document: systemWillShutdown

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1811071-systemwillshutdown
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1811071-systemwillshutdown
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# systemWillShutdown

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Notifies members of the power plane of system shutdown and restart.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual void systemWillShutdown(
 IOOptionBitsspecifier ); 
```

## Parameters

- `specifier`: `kIOMessageSystemWillPowerOff` or `kIOMessageSystemWillRestart`.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

This function is called for all members of the power plane in leaf-to-root order. If a subclass needs to wait for a pending I/O, then the call to `systemWillShutdown` should be postponed until the I/O completes.

Any power managed driver (which has called joinPMtree to join the power plane) interested in taking action at system shutdown or restart should override this method.

Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# temperatureCriticalForZone

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Alerts a driver to a critical temperature in some thermal zone.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual IOReturn temperatureCriticalForZone(
 IOService *whichZone ) __attribute__((deprecated)); 
```

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

This call is unused by power management. It is not intended to be called or overridden.

# Document: temporaryPowerClampOn

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1811099-temporarypowerclampon
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1811099-temporarypowerclampon
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# temporaryPowerClampOn

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

A driver calls this method to hold itself in the highest power state until it has children.

## Declaration

```objectivec
IOReturn temporaryPowerClampOn(
 void ); 
```

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

A return code that can be ignored by the caller.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Use `temporaryPowerClampOn` to hold your driver in its highest power state while waiting for child devices to attach. After children have attached, the clamp is released and the device's power state is controlled by the children's requirements.

# Document: terminate

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1811110-terminate
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1811110-terminate
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# terminate

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Makes an IOService object inactive and begins its destruction.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual bool terminate(
 IOOptionBits options = 0 ); 
```

## Parameters

- `options`: In most cases no options are needed. `kIOServiceSynchronous` may be passed to cause `terminate` to not return until the service is finalized.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Registering an IOService object informs possible clients of its existance and instantiates drivers that may be used with it; `terminate` involves the opposite process of informing clients that an IOService object is no longer able to be used and will be destroyed. By default, if any client has the service open, `terminate` fails. If the `kIOServiceRequired` flag is passed however, `terminate` will be successful though further progress in the destruction of the IOService object will not proceed until the last client has closed it. The service will be made inactive immediately upon successful termination, and all its clients will be notified via their message method with a message of type `kIOMessageServiceIsTerminated`. Both these actions take place on the caller's thread. After the IOService object is made inactive, further matching or attach calls will fail on it. Each client has its stop method called upon their close of an inactive IOService object , or on its termination if they do not have it open. After `stop`, detach is called in each client. When all clients have been detached, the finalize method is called in the inactive service. The termination process is inherently asynchronous because it will be deferred until all clients have chosen to close.

# Document: terminateClient

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1811121-terminateclient
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1811121-terminateclient
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# terminateClient

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Passes a termination up the stack.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual bool terminateClient(
 IOService *client,
 IOOptionBitsoptions ); 
```

## Parameters

- `client`: The client of the terminated provider.
- `options`: Options originally passed to terminate, plus `kIOServiceRecursing`.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

result of the terminate request on the client.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

When an IOService object is made inactive the default behavior is to also make any of its clients that have it as their only provider inactive, in this way recursing the termination up the driver stack. This method allows a terminated IOService object to override this behavior. Note the client may also override this behavior by overriding its terminate method.

Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# unlockForArbitration

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Unlocks an IOService obkect after a successful lockForArbitration.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual void unlockForArbitration(
 void ); 
```

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

A thread granted exclusive access to an IOService object should release it with `unlockForArbitration`.

# Document: unregisterInterrupt

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1811142-unregisterinterrupt
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1811142-unregisterinterrupt
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# unregisterInterrupt

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Removes a C function interrupt handler for a device supplying hardware interrupts.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual IOReturn unregisterInterrupt(
 intsource); 
```

## Parameters

- `source`: The index of the interrupt source in the device.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

An IOReturn code (`kIOReturnNoInterrupt` is returned if the source is not valid).

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

This method removes a C function interrupt handler previously installed with registerInterrupt.

# updateReport

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

request current data for the specified channels

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual IOReturn updateReport(
 IOReportChannelList *channels, 
 IOReportUpdateActionaction, 
 void *result, 
 void *destination); 
```

## Parameters

- `channels`: \- channels to be updated
- `action`: \- type/style of update
- `result`: \- returned details about what was updated
- `destination`: \- destination for this update (action-specific)

# Document: waitForMatchingService

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1811164-waitformatchingservice
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1811164-waitformatchingservice
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# waitForMatchingService

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Waits for a matching to service to be published.

## Declaration

```objectivec
static IOService * waitForMatchingService(
 OSDictionary *matching, 
 uint64_t timeout = timeout); 
```

## Parameters

- `matching`: The matching dictionary describing the desired IOService object. (Does not consume a reference of the matching dictionary - differs from waitForService() which does consume a reference on the matching dictionary.)
- `timeout`: The maximum time to wait in nanoseconds. Default is to wait forever.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

A published IOService object matching the supplied dictionary. waitForMatchingService returns a reference to the IOService which should be released by the caller. (Differs from waitForService() which does not retain the returned object.)

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Provides a method of waiting for an IOService object matching the supplied matching dictionary to be registered and fully matched.

# Document: waitForService

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1811172-waitforservice
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1811172-waitforservice
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# waitForService

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Deprecated use waitForMatchingService(). Waits for a matching to service to be published.

## Declaration

```objectivec
static IOService * waitForService(
 OSDictionary *matching, 
 mach_timespec_t *timeout = 0); 
```

## Parameters

- `matching`: The matching dictionary describing the desired IOService object. `waitForService` consumes one reference of the matching dictionary.
- `timeout`: The maximum time to wait.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

A published IOService object matching the supplied dictionary.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Provides a method of waiting for an IOService object matching the supplied matching dictionary to be registered and fully matched.

# Document: waitQuiet

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1811184-waitquiet
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1811184-waitquiet
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# waitQuiet

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Waits for an IOService object's `busyState` to be zero.

## Declaration

```objectivec
IOReturn waitQuiet(
 uint64_t timeout = timeout); 
```

## Parameters

- `timeout`: The maximum time to wait in nanoseconds. Default is to wait forever.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

Returns an error code if Mach synchronization primitives fail, `kIOReturnTimeout`, or `kIOReturnSuccess`.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Blocks the caller until an IOService object is non busy.

# Document: willTerminate

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1811202-willterminate
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1811202-willterminate
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# willTerminate

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Passes a termination up the stack.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual bool willTerminate(
 IOService *provider,
 IOOptionBitsoptions ); 
```

## Parameters

- `provider`: The terminated provider of this object.
- `options`: Options originally passed to terminate.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

`true`.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Notification that a provider has been terminated, sent before recursing up the stack, in root-to-leaf order.

# youAreRoot

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Informs power management which IOService object is the power plane root.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual IOReturn youAreRoot(
 void ) __attribute__((deprecated)); 
```

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

This call is handled internally by power management. It is not intended to be overridden or called by drivers.

# Document: ChangePowerState

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/3180692-changepowerstate
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/3180692-changepowerstate
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# ChangePowerState

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** DriverKit, Kernel  
**Kind:** Instance Method  
**Availability:** DriverKit 19.0+ · macOS 10.15+

Changes the device's power state to the specified level.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual kern_return_t ChangePowerState(uint32_t powerFlags);
```

```objectivec
kern_return_t ChangePowerState(uint32_t powerFlags, OSDispatchMethod supermethod);
```

## Parameters

- `powerFlags`: The new power state for the device. Typically, you specify only [kIOServicePowerCapabilityLow](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/driverkit/kioservicepowercapabilitylow) for this parameter. For a list of all possible values, see [Service Power Capabilities](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/driverkit/3325571-service_power_capabilities).

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

[kIOReturnSuccess](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/driverkit/kioreturnsuccess) on success, or another value if an error occurs. For a list of error codes, see [Error Codes](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/driverkit/error-codes).

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

If the new state is different than the device's current state, this method places an asynchronous request to change the state to the new value. If the change is successful, the system subsequently calls the [SetPowerState](3180704-setpowerstate.md) method of your service.

## See Also

### Responding to Power-Level Changes

- [SetPowerState](3180704-setpowerstate.md): Updates the service in response to power-related changes for a provider.
- [Service Power Capabilities](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/driverkit/3325571-service_power_capabilities): Constants that indicate the power state of a device.

# Document: Start

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/3180710-start
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/3180710-start
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# Start

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** DriverKit, Kernel  
**Kind:** Instance Method  
**Availability:** DriverKit 19.0+ · macOS 10.15+

Starts the current service and associates it with the specified provider.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual kern_return_t Start(IOService *provider);
```

```objectivec
kern_return_t Start(IOService *provider, OSDispatchMethod supermethod);
```

## Parameters

- `provider`: The provider object that matches the current service. Cast this object to the class you expect. The system retains this object for the duration of your [Start](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/serialdriverkit/iouserserial/start) method. The system continues to retain the object if your service starts successfully, releasing it only after calling your service's [Stop](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/serialdriverkit/iouserserial/stop) method.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

[kIOReturnSuccess](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/driverkit/kioreturnsuccess) on success, or another value if an error occurs. For a list of error codes, see [Error Codes](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/driverkit/error-codes).

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

After successfully matching the specified `provider` to your driver's service, the system instantiates your service object and calls this method. Use this method to configure your driver's data structures and setup the associated hardware. You might also store a reference to the `provider` object for later use. After you configure your driver, call the [RegisterService](3180701-registerservice.md) method to let the system know your service is running.

Always call `super` early in your implementation of this method.

## See Also

### Running the Service

- [init](3180717-init.md): Handles the basic initialization of the service.
- [Stop](3180713-stop.md): Stops the service associated with the specified provider.
- [free](3180716-free.md): Performs any final cleanup for the service.

# Document: Stop

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/3180713-stop
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/3180713-stop
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# Stop

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** DriverKit, Kernel  
**Kind:** Instance Method  
**Availability:** DriverKit 19.0+ · macOS 10.15+

Stops the service associated with the specified provider.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual kern_return_t Stop(IOService *provider);
```

```objectivec
kern_return_t Stop(IOService *provider, OSDispatchMethod supermethod);
```

## Parameters

- `provider`: The provider associated with the current service. This object is the same one that the system previously passed to your service's [Start](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/serialdriverkit/iouserserial/start) method.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

[kIOReturnSuccess](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/driverkit/kioreturnsuccess) on success, or another value if an error occurs. For a list of error codes, see [Error Codes](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/driverkit/error-codes).

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

Before terminating the object in `provider`, the system calls this method to stop the service associated with that object. Use your implementation of this method to stop all activity and put your driver in a quiescent state. If your driver has any in-progress asynchronous tasks, cancel those tasks and wait for DriverKit to call the associated cancellation handler before calling the `super` version of this method. 

Call `super` at the end of your implementation. After you call `super`, it is a programmer error to access the `provider` object.

Don't use this method to release your `ivars` structure; use the [free](3180716-free.md) method instead.

## See Also

### Running the Service

- [init](3180717-init.md): Handles the basic initialization of the service.
- [Start](3180710-start.md): Starts the current service and associates it with the specified provider.
- [free](3180716-free.md): Performs any final cleanup for the service.

# Document: init

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/3180717-init
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/3180717-init
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# init

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** DriverKit, Kernel  
**Kind:** Instance Method  
**Availability:** DriverKit 19.0+ · macOS 10.15+

## Declaration

```objectivec

```

```objectivec
virtual bool init(IORegistryEntry *from, const IORegistryPlane *inPlane);
```

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

`true` if initialization was successful, or `false` if an error occurred.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

The system calls this method shortly after it instantiates your custom [IOService](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/driverkit/ioservice) subclass, and before it calls the [Start](3180710-start.md) method of your service. Limit the work you do in this method to simple tasks that must occur before your service starts. For example, use this method to allocate memory for your `ivars` structure.

Always call `super` early in your implementation of this method.

# Document: IOServiceInterestHandler

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioserviceinteresthandler
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioserviceinteresthandler
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# IOServiceInterestHandler

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Type Alias  
**Availability:** macOS 10.0+

## Declaration

```objectivec
typedef IOReturn (*IOServiceInterestHandler)(void *target, void *refCon, UInt32 messageType, IOService *provider, void *messageArgument, vm_size_t argSize);
```

## Parameters

- `target`: Reference supplied when the notification was registered.
- `refCon`: Reference constant supplied when the notification was registered.
- `messageType`: Type of the message - IOKit defined in IOKit/IOMessage.h or family specific.
- `provider`: The IOService object who is delivering the notification. It is retained for the duration of the handler's invocation and doesn't need to be released by the handler.
- `messageArgument`: An argument for message, dependent on its type.
- `argSize`: Non zero if the argument represents a struct of that size, used when delivering messages outside the kernel.

# Document: IOServiceNotificationHandler

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservicenotificationhandler
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservicenotificationhandler
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# IOServiceNotificationHandler

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Type Alias  
**Availability:** macOS 10.0+

## Declaration

```objectivec
typedef bool (*IOServiceNotificationHandler)(void *target, void *refCon, IOService *newService);
```

## Parameters

- `target`: Reference supplied when the notification was registered.
- `refCon`: Reference constant supplied when the notification was registered.
- `newService`: The IOService object the notification is delivering. It is retained for the duration of the handler's invocation and doesn't need to be released by the handler.
